what: The scene-quality regression: eleven reference scenes, each scored by the critic's own heuristic over frames the real sidecar rendered, and held to a floor. A score below its floor fails CI - the only signal that catches the day a change makes the output worse while the tests stay green.
how: scripts/motion/scene-quality.py renders each storyboard at the sampled instants (a plate under each comp, from the same deterministic generators the multi-layer example's assets come from), measures the frames with the sense layer's own pixel metrics, scores with sense.heuristic (no audio: still frames carry none, so every scene's sound axis sits at the same unmeasured 5.5), and compares to the floor. --refresh re-measures and prints these rows.
floors: A floor sits 0.4 under the measured score: far enough that renderer jitter - a dHash bit, a rounding step - cannot fail it, close enough that a real regression - a font that stopped loading, an entrance that stopped entering, a colour that went grey, a plate that stopped compositing - does. Re-measure with --refresh when a change moves a score ON PURPOSE, and say in the commit why the scene got better or worse.
measured_at: measured on the harness' first run, 2026-11-01, geneva 1.6.0, the sidecar pinned by scripts/ci/deps.lock
